items.title: Xbox 25th Anniversary Console Stock Sells Out in Seconds, Sparking Fan Fury Over Scalping and Limited Supply
items.description: Fans have been left furious by Microsoft's launch of its 25th Anniversary Xbox Series X console, which sold out within seconds online. Now, scalpers are cashing in.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Fans have been left furious by Microsoft's handling of its 25th Anniversary Xbox Series X console launch, after stock sold out within seconds online.

Social media is awash with reports from players who attempted to purchase one of the company's snazzy translucent green 25th Anniversary consoles from the Microsoft Store, only for stock to sell out before they could finish making their order.

To be fair, Microsoft had previously stated it would only have a "limited number" of consoles to sell at launch. In a social media post earlier this week, the company noted that availability would begin at midnight Eastern time and that quantities and availability would "vary by market and retailer."

Still, numerous fans were left empty-handed, or angered by retailers such as GameStop taking advantage of the low stock situation by selling the $999 console at a huge markup. For a time, GameStop was shifting its stock allocation at the eye-watering price of $4,950, although even this now appears to have sold out.

Much of the criticism has been levied against Microsoft itself, however, for only making a small number of consoles available and for not having a better online queueing system available. Some fans have suggested that purchases could have been limited to customers with Xbox accounts to prove their legitimacy and limit bulk buying. This option could have even been tightened further to offer the console first to Xbox's most dedicated fans — perhaps those with older account status, or those who have collected a certain amount of Gamerscore.

Whatever the potential solution, however, Microsoft appears to have just let its stock go on sale via a first-come, first-serve basis. Inevitably, this has lead to numerous consoles being placed upon eBay at a notable markup. Looking online this morning, IGN has seen dozens of Xbox 25th Anniversary consoles that have already been sold through eBay for $1,500, and up to $2,500.

"At this point I don't even care anymore," one Xbox fan wrote in a post on X/Twitter. "I tried back in August, I tried last night and I tried tonight. Yea im upset I cant get one of these due to scalpers but, I just cant find it in myself to care anymore. I love Xbox, but what a mess."

"It's all a joke," another fan added, comparing the launch to Sony's similar PS5 anniversary consoles. "They’re made specifically for bots, scalpers and to be backdoored. No genuine fans actually get these."

"I have been a Xbox loyal fan for 20+ years and I can't even get my hands on this," added another fan. "I stayed up and have been trying to get one since 12pm YESTERDAY. You do nothing for the loyals and let these scalpers and bots take them all. Nothing restocked. When I ended up getting one in my cart the f***ing website just loaded and loaded until it disappeared. Just a f***ing shame. Beyond pissed off rn."

Last month, Xbox boss Asha Sharma insisted that falling sales of Xbox consoles had been hampered by supply constraints, and that there was "more demand than consoles available."

items.title: Dragon Age Fans Save One of the Series' Most Beloved Features
items.description: Dragon Age fans have saved one of the series’ most beloved features: being able to import your world states in each game.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Dragon Age fans have saved one of the series’ most beloved features: being able to import your world states in each game.

With the Mass Effect trilogy, this was simple: just play through the series on the same console, and your saves are automatically carried over. The same was true going from Dragon Age: Origins into Dragon Age 2. But by the time Dragon Age: Inquisition rolled around in 2014, a new console generation was upon us, so BioWare had to get creative.

This is when we get the Dragon Age Keep. This website connects to your EA account and keeps track of all the decisions you made in the previous games. Or, you can just input whatever decisions you want manually. You can then import this crafted world state into Dragon Age: Inquisition and see your previous choices reflected in the game.

I am sure many of you can already see the problem with this system: it’s an online service that needs to be maintained. True enough, the Dragon Age Keep experiences fairly frequent outages, during which time no one can start a new Inquisition run with their choices carried over.

Now that EA has shut down BioWare, it’s unclear what will happen if the Keep goes offline again, or how long EA plans to keep it going. Thankfully, fans already have a solution, at least if you’re on PC. A couple of modders have released user-friendly ways to adjust the game files so your choices still carry over, even if EA pulls the plug on the Dragon Age Keep.

First up, there’s Thedas World State Studio - Dragon Age Keep Utility by Nexus Mods user anshela. This gives you an offline alternative to the Keep, letting you input your choices in the same tapestry format you would in the online version.

This is much more user-friendly than previous methods of editing your world state on PC. As anyone who has tried will tell you, modding Inquisition is a nightmare thanks to the Frostbite engine, but this tool should make it much more accessible.

The modder says they were already working on this before the BioWare news hit, and the fact that it is ready now is just “good/bad timing." Indeed it is, because the next Dragon Age Keep outage could be the last.

Right now, the mod files have been “quarantined” while Nexus approves the latest version, so it can’t be downloaded just yet. But once it’s up and running again, it should work just fine, judging from the response from users so far.

This isn’t the only mod you’ll need if the servers go offline. The closest thing Inquisition has to New Game Plus lets you port almost all of your unlocks into future playthroughs, but for whatever reason, this also requires the Keep to be up, even though it’s only dealing with things you’ve unlocked in Inquisition.

That is where Thedas Chronicle - World State and Golden Nug Fix by TP1231 has us covered. This will let you access the Golden Nug statue that activates item transfers even if the servers are down. As the name suggests, it will also let you play with your imported world state when the Keep is offline, but you will still need the world state that you made while the servers are up.

While it’s great to see fans get these solutions out before EA potentially pulls the plug, it is no wonder that BioWare didn’t want to risk this happening ever again. Instead, Dragon Age: The Veilguard had us input previous choices in the game itself, so it could be played offline. Granted, we had far fewer options to carry over that time around, much to the frustration of fans, but at least it means we won’t have to go through this again.

In the meantime, BioWare fans are currently fighting to save the studio’s IPs. Most notably, the Save Mass Effect movement has amassed thousands of supporters, as they urge EA to do something with the IP, rather than let the series die.

items.title: After Giving Away Thousands of Dollars in Cosmetics, Fortnite is Teasing a Big Reveal For Captain X, Its Mysterious Masked Treasure Man — With Fan Guesses Ranging From Mr Beast to Obama
items.description: Fortnite is teasing a big reveal for its upcoming December 5 live event, which will reveal the identity of mysterious new character Captain X.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Fortnite is teasing a big reveal for its upcoming December 5 live event, which will reveal the identity of mysterious new character Captain X.

The game has previously employed big-name stars such as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson and Brie Larson to portray notable in-game characters, and appears to be on the cusp of unveiling yet another casting of some significance.

Captain X made their debut at the beginning of Fortnite's current treasure-hunting mini-season, though their motives are currently unclear. As Fortnite's heroes hunt a fresh macguffin, Captain X has seemingly allowed them to make steady progress, while the game's story has suggested the character could also simply be letting players do their legwork instead, before swooping in to steal the prize.

At the same time, Fortnite itself has introduced a treasure hunting mechanic where players can win a fortnight of free access to the game's lucrative Item Shop — something that has sent concurrent player numbers soaring into the millions (all timed to cushion the blow of GTA 6's launch.)

Whether Captain X turns out to be friend or foe remains unclear, as does their relation to the game's wider storyline. This currently features a roster of surviving heroes from much of the game's past decade returning to face down Geno, Fortnite's uber Big Bad from the days when Epic Games' former creative boss Donald Mustard was still in charge of the storyline.

Should Geno actually be defeated, finally, will Captain X be revealed as the next major threat? Or perhaps they will be a new hero for players to follow, should Jonesy finally fall in battle?

Whatever is the case, Epic Games is clearly now teasing that there's more to Captain X than meets the eye. Last night at the Streamer Awards 2026, Captain X turned up in person wearing a mask to deliver a hand-written note confirming that they would be fully unveiled on December 5 — the date of Fortnite's next Chapter-ending live event.

Genuine question. Who could this possibly be that would be both exciting to see and fitting for Captain X's character. Like, the Foundation being The Rock only worked because there was a year of buildup and a lack of notable names in Fortnite. We have like everyone in the game now.

Not even trying to be miserable or anything here, I'm just absolutely lost as to who he(?) could possibly be.

— kat (@kattylotl) November 13, 2026

Currently, Captain X has only appeared in-game with their face covered, while their dialogue has been disguised with a heavy voice filter. (Players previously worked out that The Rock was playing a key character pretty quickly from his voice lines, even though he remained masked for almost a year — something that has not yet happened this time around.)

But who is it under the mask? Fans are speculating that the character will be played by a well-known actor or celebrity, with many suspecting that MrBeast has been brought on board. The YouTube star is already available in Fortnite as a character skin, and Captain X's ability to dole out hugely valuable prizes certainly lines up with MrBeast's usual shtick. Other fans have suggested the X is actually a clue this will be a new character played by Elon Musk, which seems extremely unlikely. And even less possibly, others have rounded on the idea that this seemingly generous person is actually President Barack Obama — which would certainly be a booking.

If you can tear yourself away from GTA 6 in time for December's Fortnite live event, we'll find out for sure what's going on, in just under a month's time.

items.title: Microsoft Struggling to Fix Global System Outage Impacting Email Systems and More, Admits Initial Repairs 'Not Taking as Expected'
items.description: Microsoft is struggling to fix a prolonged systems outage that has hindered access to online services including Outlook and Teams.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Microsoft is struggling to fix a prolonged systems outage that has hindered access to online services including Outlook and Teams.

On the upside, AI tool Copilot has also been impacted.

For more than 12 hours, users around the world have been reporting an inability to access email accounts, instant messaging systems, and documents via OneDrive and Office365. No Xbox services are believed to be offline, however.

Microsoft was quick to acknowledge the problem and admit that it was suffering from issues with its server capabilities, with "elevated load across multiple regions." Attempts to solve this were initially unsuccessful, however, as the company reported its fixes were "not taking as expected."

"We've monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected," Microsoft said in a lengthy thread on X/Twitter. "We're identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances."

Hours later, Microsoft seemed to have changed tack and was now trying to carve out the impacted servers completely as it struggled to make progress.

"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," the company then stated. "We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."

Why is this happening? Microsoft has blamed a number of servers becoming "unexpectedly unavailable", adding strain to its remaining capacity, rather than any sudden increase in traffic. That would suggest this is not a targeted DDOS attack, and indeed, Microsoft exec Charles LaManna has confirmed "there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity."

We'll update again when there's been further developments. In the meantime, hopefully you're having a quiet day at work or school.

Photo Illustration by Scott Olson/Getty Images.

items.title: GTA 6's Burger Shot Restaurant Is Expanding Across Florida With Real Meals Inspired by the Game
items.description: GTA 6's fast-food hamburger chain, Burger Shot, is expanding with new locations across Florida starting this weekend thanks to a collaboration with Skinny Louie.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6's fast-food hamburger chain, Burger Shot, is expanding with new locations across Florida starting this weekend thanks to a collaboration with Skinny Louie.

Last month, Burger Shot became available at the Kaseya Center, allowing fans to try the real version of the in-game restaurant during Miami Heat games, courtesy of a partnership with a fast-food joint known as Skinny Louie. The chain is now expanding this activation through its standalone stores across Florida. From November 13 to December 31, stores will feature Burger Shot signage, uniforms, and, of course, a menu themed after items in the game.

You can take a look at the menu and some images of the food below.

Skinny Louie's Burger Shot Menu

THE BLEEDER — TRIPLE
Three 100% Black Angus smash patties with yellow American cheese, crispy bacon, pickles, BBQ sauce, and ketchup.

BURGER SHOT — SINGLE

One 100% Black Angus smash patty with yellow American cheese, shredded lettuce, diced raw onions, and Burger Shot sauce.

BURGER SHOT — DOUBLE
Two 100% Black Angus smash patties with yellow American cheese, shredded lettuce, diced raw onions, and Burger Shot sauce.

CARAMEL MILKSHAKE

All of this just goes to show how big GTA 6 has gotten. There aren't many video game franchises that could completely command and rebrand a chain of restaurants, but GTA 6 certainly has that power. The game is already the most pre-ordered title in the history of Xbox and PlayStation's digital stores, and analysts estimate that the game has generated $1 billion in revenue ahead of launch.

GTA 6 will officially release next week on November 19 and players can start pre-loading right now. Rockstar has also been trickling out small clips of in-game footage, giving players a taste of what's to come when they load in to Vice City next week.

items.title: Wolfenstein 3 Confirmed to Be in Development at MachineGames
items.description: As part of the Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at Xbox Fanfest in Seattle today, developer MachineGames confirmed what had long been rumored: that Wolfenstein 3 is in development.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
As part of the Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at Xbox Fanfest in Seattle today, developer MachineGames confirmed what had long been rumored: that Wolfenstein 3 is in development.

MachineGames will once again be developing it. Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus was released to rave reviews in 2017, but MachineGames then put the series on hold to develop 2024's absolutely stellar Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

But now, Wolfenstein is back on the front burner at the Swedish studio. "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at Machine Games," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed on X. "One of gaming’s most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more."

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvh

— ASHA (@asha_shar) November 12, 2026

MachineGames added on to Sharma's post, which shows a page of the Wolfenstein 3 script, saying simply, "His reputation precedes him," referring to the action described on the script page. "Wolfenstein 3 is in production." The developers also confirmed that actors Brian Bloom (as B.J. Blazkowicz) and Debra Wilson (as Grace Walker) will return via a photo of the pair in the developer's motion-capture studio.

Wolfenstein 3 shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Last year, in an interview with Noclip, MachineGames studio head Jerk Gustafsson said the team had "always seen [BJ's story] as a trilogy," adding: "That journey for BJ, even during those first weeks at [id Software], when we mapped out New Order — we still had the plan for at least [BJ], what would happen in the second one and what would happen in the third one.

"I think that's important to say, because⁠ — at least, I hope ⁠— we're not done with Wolfenstein yet. We have a story to tell."

That's not all that Wolfenstein fans have to look forward to, as the pioneering first-person shooter series is also being developed into a TV series at Amazon. Xbox's official 25th anniversary is this Sunday, November 15.

items.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Reportedly Had Third Affair With Another Employee
items.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned today amid a scandal involving an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and an executive that reported to him. Now, it's been reported that Huang allegedly had an affair with a second employee.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned today amid a scandal involving an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and an executive that reported to him. Now, it's been reported that Huang allegedly had an affair with a second employee.

Huang allegedly had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two sources inside Nvidia and reported by Reuters. However, Reuters hasn't named the second employee, and attempts to reach her were not successful.

This third revelation comes just hours after Huang resigned from Nvidia, following an internal investigation that kicked off on Sunday. Huang himself came out and admitted to one of the affairs in a letter sent to Nvidia staff and obtained by The BBC. Then, following a meeting where Nvidia's board weighed ousting Huang, the former CEO resigned.

In the meantime, Nvidia's board has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while the company searches for a new leader. Nvidia is considering both internal and external applicants, but there has been talk that Apple Senior Vice President of Hardware Technlogy Johny Srouji is being considered for the role, according to MacRumors.

As for Huang itself, it's not clear where he's going to end up, or what he's going to do going forward. Last night, Elon Musk posted on X that it "would be an honor" to hire Huang... but it's doubtful that he'd end up at any of Musk's companies.

Either way, Huang has been leading Nvidia since 1993, and has seen the company grow from being a niche gaming hardware company to the backbone of the entire AI industry. His resignation is going to send shockwaves throughout the entire tech biz. One of the biggest casualties might end up being PC gaming altogether. After all, Nvidia makes up for a massive 73% of Steam's install base, according to the latest Steam Hardware survey, but the company still dropped gaming from its earnings reports earlier this year. And, now with Jensen's departure, it's unlikely that PC hardware is going to get the same level of support.

Photo by Joel Saget / AFP via Getty Images.

items.title: Valheim Is Getting a Comic Book Series, and It Looks Badass
items.description: Valheim is expanding beyond video games once again, this time with an official comic book series featuring an impressive lineup of talent from Marvel, DC, television, and animation.
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Valheim is expanding beyond video games once again, this time with an official comic book series featuring an impressive lineup of talent from Marvel, DC, television, and animation.

Developer Iron Gate Studio has teamed up with GUNGNIR Books and MOOD Publishing to bring its Viking survival game to comics, with the first release planned for the first quarter of 2027. The multi-issue series will feature original stories set in the world of Valheim, rather than simply retelling the events of the game.

The writing team certainly has a pretty impressive portfolio that bodes well for the series. It includes Steve Orlando (Wonder Woman, Avengers), Deric A. Hughes and Ben Raab (Quantum Leap), J. Holtham (The Handmaid's Tale, Supergirl), Brea Grant (12 Hour Shift), Tim Sheridan (Masters of the Universe), and Olan Rogers (Final Space). They're joined by TD Orel, Chris Klian, Andrew Sanders, and GUNGNIR Books founder Matthew Medney.

On the art side, Scott Oakley, Vanessa Del Rey, Lucas Pereira, and Mario Del Pennino are among the confirmed artists, with Mohamad Samah overseeing production design. More talent is expected to be announced.

According to the announcement, the series will explore the mythology of Valheim's mysterious tenth Norse realm, introducing new adventures and perspectives on its gods, monsters, and dangerous environments. Expect plenty of exploration, survival, and presumably some very unfortunate encounters with the local wildlife.

This is Valheim, and we're going to make it epic.

“Valheim is one of those rare worlds that feels like it existed long before we ever discovered it. There are gods, monsters, entire civilizations, and a mythology so rich that the stories we can tell feel almost endless," said Matthew Medney from GUNGNIR Books. "For us, the opportunity to work alongside Iron Gate and MOOD Publishing to bring this universe into comics is extraordinary. And we've assembled an absolute army of creative talent to do it. We're not interested in simply retelling what millions of players have already experienced. We want to explore the legends that haven't been told, the corners of this world that haven't been seen, and create something that feels worthy of the incredible universe Iron Gate built. This is Valheim, and we're going to make it epic."

The comic marks another expansion for Valheim, which has now sold more than 17 million copies worldwide since launching into Steam Early Access in February 2021. The game has already made the jump to tabletop gaming with Valheim: The Board Game, also developed in partnership with MOOD Publishing.

For now, there's no specific release date beyond Q1 2027, and details about individual issues, collectible editions, and how fans can get involved are still to come. In the meantime, Valheim players can look forward to exploring the tenth realm without having to worry about keeping their food buffs topped up. Which, frankly, sounds rather nice.

items.title: Fable Drops Four Minutes of New Gameplay
items.description: Four minutes of new Fable gameplay has been released by Xbox, showing off more of the game's combat.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Four minutes of new Fable gameplay has been released by Xbox, showing off more of the game's combat.

The footage was released personally by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma as part of a larger celebration for the company's 25th anniversary. The gameplay shows off a bunch of combat, highlighting not only standard swordplay, but also ranged attacks and unique moves that can be performed using magic. The gameplay was captured on PC using ultra graphics settings and concludes with the protagonist stumbling upon an incredibly sinister-looking tomb or coffin.

Fable was, of course, meant to have been released this fall. However, Xbox made the smart decision to delay the game to February. Although the team says the delay wasn't done specifically in an effort to avoid GTA 6, it was likely a nice benefit. Microsoft still had plenty of releases this autumn thanks to Modern Warfare 4 and Gears of War: E-Day, so it was wise to give Fable some more room to breathe. The game was announced all the way back in 2020, but has been in some form of development at Playground Games for nearly a decade.

Forza Horizon studio Playground Games is leading the charge on the title, though it has recruited a bunch of talent from around the industry so that it is well-equipped to build an RPG. Fable is one of the most anticipated games on Xbox's slate, partially because it's one of the most beloved RPG franchises out there, and Microsoft is looking for a big win in the AAA space outside of shooters.

Fable is also coming to PS5, as it had been previously announced for the platform. It'll be interesting to see what happens if the game performs well on the platform. Xbox is trying to lean more into exclusivity, but it unfortunately didn't seem to pay off for Gears of War: E-Day. Here's hoping Fable is worth the wait and pays off on Microsoft's investments.

Fable will release on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC on February 23.

items.title: ‘Maybe We’ve Gone a Step Too Far’ — Ocarina of Time Remake Producer Reveals the Game's ReDeads Were Originally Supposed to Be Even Scarier
items.description: Producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained why the development team behind the Ocarina of Time Remake toned down the ReDeads to make them less scary.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained why the development team behind the Ocarina of Time Remake toned down the ReDeads to make them less scary.

If you grew up playing the original Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64, you were probably traumatized by some of the game’s famously frightening enemies like the Gibdos, ReDeads, and Dead Hands. These last two were particularly terrifying for young players at the time — partially because we were still kids, and partially due to the N64’s graphical limitations that forced our minds to fill in the visual gaps in the monsters’ designs.

These enemies were a particular talking point when the Remake was first announced. Some players were doubtful that this new game could truly capture the terror of the original monsters, since a) it’s a game that’s also supposed to appeal to children and b) the updated graphics of modern Nintendo consoles don’t necessarily allow for the ‘fear of the unknown’ phenomena afforded to low-fidelity titles like 1999's Silent Hill. (There’s an entire genre of indie horror games that pursue this aesthetic for a reason, after all.)

Speaking with Gamespot, producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained that the Remake’s updated graphics actually made the ReDeads extremely scary at first. And while the development team was supposedly enthusiastic about this aspect of the project, he and fellow producer Eiji Aonuma felt that this detail wasn’t necessarily true to the original experience of the first game.

"With this remake, the graphics are a lot improved, and so the ReDead – the sound, the graphics, and the movement – ended up being very, very scary,” Fujibayashi said. “And the staff wanted to make this in service of making a good gameplay experience. But from our perspective, taking a step back, we felt like, ‘Let's remember the experience that we don't want to change, and taking that into consideration, maybe we've gone a step too far, so let's dial it back.’"

That being said, plenty of players feel that the Remake’s ReDeads are still sufficiently terrifying. Social media is rife with hilarious reactions from fans’ first encounters with the enemies, with both Western and Japanese players having a “nope, f**k this,” mentality after first coming across them in the game.

これが令和のリーデッド

オリジナルのポリゴンデザインよりグロテスクになっててチビる

#時のオカリナ https://t.co/9k1XpH3NZs

— 凌ちゃん (@ryochan_642) November 5, 2026

The ReDeads have eyes this time https://t.co/UBBqZf41SW

— Boundary Break (@BoundaryBreak) November 7, 2026

THEY RUN AT YOU NOW???? https://t.co/fqkgDWaoU8

— Torino (@Torinotortolini) November 5, 2026

Others are hopeful that, should other Zelda remakes get produced, Nintendo makes its other enemies equally scary — especially since these new ReDeads are far more mobile than their predecessors.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has, perhaps unsurprisingly, proven to be a smash hit for Nintendo; the game sold over five million copies in just four days and released to rave reviews from both fans and critics. IGN’s Logan Plant scored the title a glowing 9 out of 10, praising it for “skillfully melding the world and dungeon design of classic Zeldas with the movement and presentation of its more recent games, creating both a beautiful retelling of a legend and a rich adventure that stands on its own.”

items.title: Doom Developer id Software Confirms Work on New Game, Will Be Directed by Hugo Martin
items.description: At Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at its Fan Fest event in Seattle, id Software confirmed that it is working on a new game, wrapping up last year's Doom: The Dark Ages with the release of the upcoming Slaughter Mode on November 16.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
At Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at its Fan Fest event in Seattle, id Software confirmed that it is working on a new game, wrapping up last year's Doom: The Dark Ages with the release of the upcoming Slaughter Mode on November 16.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma made the announcement on her X account, posting, "Few studios have shaped the first-person shooter genre as much as id Software. Slaughter Mode comes to DOOM: The Dark Ages | Revelations on November 16, and the team is already working on its next game." id itself also posted, saying, "We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on."

Whether that next project is more Doom, or perhaps id returning to its other big franchise, Quake, remains to be seen. Or it might be neither of those and could be something new entirely. Although it's worth noting that id Software is under Xbox's Bethesda arm, and Bethesda boss Jill Braff recently told its development teams that "we are shifting from a planning model primarily centered on what's next for each independent studio to one that focuses on our strongest franchises and determining the content roadmap that best serves our players and Bethesda as a whole." So perhaps Quake or a fourth Doom game are the more likely options?

That remains to be seen, but what the last decade has proven is that Martin and the id Software team are very good at what they do. Doom (2016) successfully rebooted a dormant franchise, while Doom Eternal stood on its shoulders, and then Doom: The Dark Ages brought the focus back to the ground. All three were excellent.

Doom: The Dark Ages' Slaughter Mode, meanwhile, is an endless single-player mode that will be added as a free update for those who've purchased Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC, which we reviewed and loved.

items.title: AI Usage Up, PS6 and Xbox Helix Development Still Low in Newest GDC Dev Survey
items.description: GDC Festival of Gaming organizers released the data from their 15th annual game developer survey, the State of the Game Industry report. Over 2600 game developers anonymously responded, and the results show increased generative AI usage, not too many developers working on PlayStation 6 or Xbox Project Helix next-gen projects as of yet, an increase in the number of developers in a union, and more.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
GDC Festival of Gaming organizers released the data from their 15th annual game developer survey, the State of the Game Industry report. Over 2,600 game developers anonymously responded, and the results show increased generative AI usage, not too many developers working on PlayStation 6 or Xbox Project Helix next-gen projects as of yet, an increase in the number of developers in a union, and more.

"40% of game industry professionals report using generative AI tools as part of their job, up four points from the previous survey," GDC reported. "57% of AI adopters use it daily. Usage is highest among those working at mobile-only studios (70%) and those working on free-to-play games (58%). Company policy tends to vary significantly by company size, with 27% of AAA workers feeling encouraged or pressured to use generative AI, compared to only 9% of indie studio workers."

However, the report continued, "despite the industry’s increased adoption of generative AI, its use remains polarizing; 55% of respondents felt that it has a negative impact on games, which is consistent with 54% from the previous survey. Responses suggest that game industry professionals are forming nuanced stances on the topic. For instance, some respondents wrote that they see value in using generative AI tools for repetitive tasks, research, and prototyping, but others cited environmental, psychological, and societal concerns for their hesitation to use such tools. Others pondered whether generative AI could be an equalizer for marginalized and excluded groups struggling with cost, geography, or access."

Meanwhile, 10% of survey respondents are currently developing for PS6, with 8% currently working on Xbox's Project Helix. VR, augumented reality, or mixed reality game development is down to 3% of people surveyed, while Switch 2 development interest is up almost 10% to 47% this year.

Interestingly, overall support in the US for game industry worker unionization was down a tad, from 82% to 80%, but more respondents reported being part of a union – 15% this year compared to 12% last year.

Finally and unfortunately, a whopping 65% of those responding to the survey said that their mental health has suffered because of their job and the long hours – and that's for those who are still employed. A full third of respondents have been laid off in the last two years, with two-thirds of that group saying they were laid off in the past year. And sadly, more than half (54%) of those who've been laid off have yet to find another job, though not for a lack of trying: 62% say they've applied for 20 or more jobs, with over a quarter (27%) saying they've applied for over a hundred. Overall, one-fifth of survey respondents (21%) are unemployed, up from 13% in the last report.

The next Game Developers Conference: Festival of Gaming will take place in San Francisco on March 1–4, 2027.

items.title: The Game Awards 2026 are Coming to Disney+
items.description: This year’s Game Awards are coming to Disney+, where it will broadcast in addition to its usual streams on Twitch and YouTube.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
This year’s Game Awards are coming to Disney+, where it will broadcast in addition to its usual streams on Twitch and YouTube.

This partnership with Disney comes as the media monolith seeks to promote its roster of video games and game-related media projects, which Kingdom Hearts fans will note comes right on the heels of its big KH4 reveal at D23 earlier this year.

Reports from Variety state that this packed slate includes Disney Twisted-Wonderland: The Animation, as well as Death Stranding Isolations, the forthcoming anime series based on Hideo Kojima’s Death Stranding franchise. The show got its first proper trailer in late October, alongside a first look at a full-length anime film set in the Death Stranding universe, Mosquito, which is set for a theatrical release on an as-yet unannounced date.

There are already a slew of strong contenders for this year’s Game Awards, the bulk of which you can read on IGN’s Biggest Games of 2026 Playlist. Resident Evil 9, 007: First Light, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake are just a few of the heavy hitters in an already packed slate — not to mention GTA 6, which will qualify for the Awards by the skin of its teeth after its arrival on November 19.

This marks the first time The Game Awards has been offered on Disney+, which continues to expand its reach after snagging Amazon’s Prime Video last year. The program will also stream on its official profiles on Twitch, YouTube, Instagram Live, TikTok, Steam, Twitter/X, Facebook, and Kick.

Somewhat ironically, the TGAs will take place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. The show will air on Thursday, December 10 at 7:30pm ET / 4:30pm PT and will be hosted by Geoff Keighley.

The Game Awards is always rife with exciting news, reveals, performances, and sometimes, even drama, as seen last year when comedian Andrew Schulz ruffled some feathers after calling out the cast of the Mortal Kombat movie. With some big games having already been announced, like Resident Evil: Veronica and The Witcher 4, fans are more hopeful than ever that they'll get to see more of these titles at the year's most prestigious game awards event.

items.title: Doctor Doom Is Not a Tony Stark Variant in Avengers: Doomsday, Confirms Kevin Feige
items.description: Kevin Feige has confirmed that Doctor Doom is not a variant of Tony Stark in Avengers: Doomsday.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Kevin Feige has confirmed that Doctor Doom is not a variant of Tony Stark in Avengers: Doomsday.

When speaking with Empire Magazine, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige debunked the popular fan theory that Doctor Doom and Tony Stark have a shared connection in the multiverse. Fans have speculated that Doom is a "variant" of Stark, since Robert Downey Jr. plays both characters. Variants are other versions of a character across the multiverse. We've seen this with the three Spider-Men, Wolverine, and Loki, so naturally, some fans thought this may all be an elaborate way to explain how Robert Downey Jr. is also playing Doom... turns out, it's not.

“Is Steve Rogers a Johnny Storm variant?" asked Feige. "People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He’s Victor Von Doom.”

As for what Doom's whole deal is, the creative team behind the film teased what kind of energy he brings and why he is the way he is. The Russo Brothers, who are directing the film, teased that Doom has lost a child, is a "victim of trauma" and has a greater ego than Thanos. They also noted that he's a pretty terrifying presence.

"Doom is a Gothic character,” said director Joe Russo. “He says, ‘Hell answers to me,’ and he’s not kidding. He’s a very powerful character with some very dark magic, and he’s not above selling his soul to get what he wants. He’s worth being scared of.”

Robert Downey Jr. also noted that he was excited to lean into being a villain this time around, and suggested that Doom's plans have a tremendous scope to them.

"I like a bit of scorched earth,” teases Downey Jr. “Whatever you think he may be entertaining, I would ten times it, and you’ll probably be closer to the ballpark."

There's still a lot that we don't know about the film, which is just a little over a month away from being released. A recent listing on the WGA's website credited Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds for contributing to the film's script, which seems to suggest Wolverine and Deadpool may be in the film. Additionally, Marvel confirmed earlier this week that Scarlet Witch will also return in Avengers: Doomsday, though seemingly under the control of Doom himself.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18.

items.title: Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds Are Credited as Writers on Avengers: Doomsday, Creating Speculation Over Deadpool and Wolverine Roles
items.description: Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds have been credited for contributing to Avengers: Doomsday's script, sall but confirming the return of Deadpool and Wolverine.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds have been credited for contributing to Avengers: Doomsday's script, all but confirming the return of Deadpool and Wolverine.

Per an update to the Writers Guild of America's website, Avengers: Doomsday has credited a handful of people for contributing to the film's script. Although the screenplay was written by Stephen McFeely and Michael Waldron, the Additional Literary Material section confirms that Eric Pearson, Chris McKenna, Erik Sommers, Jeff Loveness, Andrew Lanham, Destin Daniel Cretton, Ryan Reynolds, and Hugh Jackman also contributed to the script. These credits are for people who are not the authors of the actual film's story, but helped punch up dialogue or did a small pass on the script.

With that said, Ryan Reynolds is well-known for helping write the Deadpool films, and it would be surprising for him to have helped out on this specific script if Deadpool wasn't in it. Although Hugh Jackman doesn't have a history as a writer, he may have also helped write Wolverine's scenes, as well, given he has spent 26 years playing the character.

The characters have been repeatedly teased to return in Doomsday by both Jackman and Reynolds, with the two doing tongue-in-cheek promos at San Diego Comic-Con and D23 over the summer. However, they haven't been explicitly confirmed to appear in the film. Since Deadpool and Wolverine were huge hits and fans have hoped to see the characters in an Avengers film for years, it only makes sense for them to finally crossover into the broader MCU.

Additionally, Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton also got a credit for Doomsday, but it's worth remembering he also directed Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings. Shang-Chi is confirmed to appear in the upcoming ensemble film, so it's more likely that his contributions are for helping write that character. It's possible Spider-Man is in the film, but it remains unclear at the moment.

Marvel also confirmed earlier this week that another major MCU character will return in Doomsday after a four-year absence. Scarlet Witch was seen at the end of VisionQuest being abducted by Doctor Doom, following her appearance in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. As a result, it seems like she may be an antagonist once again, though this time under the control of another character.

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved to Get Firefight as a Free Update
items.description: When Halo: Campaign Evolved first came out in July it did not include any multiplayer modes, but the first-person shooter remake will at least get Firefight as a free update this Winter.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
When Halo: Campaign Evolved first came out in July it did not include any multiplayer modes, but the first-person shooter remake will at least get Firefight as a free update this winter.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the returning mode in a social media post Thursday, along with a graphic showing a team of Spartans shooting a mix of Covenant and Flood enemies with various guns.

While Firefight isn't the arena competitive multiplayer that most fans had hoped from the Halo remake at launch, wave-based PvE has been a mainstay in the series since Halo 3: ODST in 2009. Essentially, you and your friends load into a map and fight increasingly difficult waves of enemies until you get overwhelmed. There's no reason to believe that this iteration is going to be any different.

Regardless of whether or not Team Deathmatch comes to Halo: Campaign Evolved, this will be the first multiplayer mode to hit the remake, which was pitched primarily as a straight-up revival of the iconic Combat Evolved campaign. Multiplayer was the major piece missing from Campaign Evolved, and this could be a sign that more multiplayer modes will be added in the future.

IGN's Halo: Combat Evolved remake gave it a 7. We said: "Halo: Campaign Evolved speaks to the series' timelessness and adds a decent set of new missions, but it's a mostly a lean retread that's more of a test run for its future with Unreal Engine."

This Firefight announcement comes as Xbox celebrates its 25th anniversary. Earlier today, Sharma looked ahead, predicting "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

As for Halo, following the summer's drastic cuts at Microsoft's gaming business, Xbox announced a significant reshuffle that saw the next mainline Halo game handed to Call of Duty developer Activision, which is spinning up a new team to work on the franchise. Mass layoffs hit Halo Studios at the same time.

items.title: New GTA 6 In-Game Footage Continues to Highlight the Game's Unbelievable Graphics
items.description: Rockstar has released yet another in-game clip from GTA 6, and like yesterday's footage, fans can't quite believe it's real.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar has released yet another in-game clip from GTA 6, and like yesterday's footage, fans can't quite believe it's real.

This morning, the Instagram account "Only in Dade" (which posts real videos from around Miami, Florida) shared a video of several flashy cars driving around. However, this footage isn't real life; it's actually GTA 6 footage.

The page posted footage of these cars sitting on GTA 6's version of Ocean Drive yesterday while a group of NPCs observed them. Yesterday's footage was actually an in-game recreation of a real video that was posted in October, showing Rockstar's real-life marketing efforts in Miami. Presumably, the new video posted today is also a recreation of a real video from when the real versions of these cars were zooming around the city.

Although the footage doesn't show much, it is an extremely impressive showcase of GTA 6's graphical fidelity. When the first clip dropped yesterday, many thought it was AI or some kind of render. However, it has since been confirmed as authentic gameplay and was reposted by Rockstar itself on Instagram. Fans have reacted to both clips in awe of the visuals, noting that the game has really outdone itself.

"Absolutely insane this is in-game," said one fan in response to the new footage. "This game isn't real, bro; there HAS to be a trap somewhere. There is no f**king way," said another fan in disbelief.

Some have even joked that if this is really how the final game looks, they're more than happy to play it at 30fps. It's clear that Rockstar traded higher performance in favor of visual fidelity, and while that may not be what some fans want, it is inevitably going to result in one of the most graphically advanced games we have ever seen.

Today officially marks exactly one week until GTA 6's release. The game is available to preload right now and it is tracking to have one of the biggest launches in entertainment history. Xbox and PlayStation both confirmed that the game is the most preordered title in the history of their respective stores, and analysts have estimated that the game has already surpassed $1 billion in sales ahead of launch.

Speaking of launch, some game developers are giving their staff the week off to play the game. Palworld developer Pocketpair is one such studio happy to provide extra holiday for the occasion. IGN's latest coverage includes speculation about a potential beloved legacy character from a previous game hiding in the latest GTA 6 trailer.

items.title: Disney Marking Star Wars 50th Anniversary With Fresh A New Hope Making Of Documentary
items.description: Disney has announced its plans for the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, which will include a fresh documentary detailing the making of A New Hope.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney has announced its plans for the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, which will include a fresh documentary detailing the making of A New Hope.

George Lucas' original Star Wars film debuted back in 1977, kicking off what would become one of the world's most popular and lucrative film and TV franchises. Half a century on, Disney+ will debut "The Hero Awakens," a brand-new documentary featuring rare archival footage from A New Hope's production, helmed by Academy Award-nominated filmmaker R.J. Cutler.

The Hero Awakens will drop via Disney+ on Star Wars' annual May 4th celebration, following the theatrical re-release of Star Wars on February 19. This will be the rarely-seen original 1977 version of the movie — back when Jabba the Hutt was not a CGI slug and Greedo actually shot first.

In terms of what's actually new for the Star Wars franchise next year, Ahsoka Season 2 will drop via Disney+ on January 20, while Star Wars: Starfighter will land in theaters on May 28.

Both are anticipated, though will arrive at a time of great uncertainty for the Star Wars franchise in general, following the decidedly mixed response to Disney's sequel trilogy, several short-lived Disney+ TV projects, and a lengthy slate of movie projects cancelled or stuck in development hell. Not even a big screen outing for The Mandalorian and Grogu this year could turn things around, as the movie set a rather disappointing record for the franchise's lowest live-action theatrical gross.

Looking further ahead, a press release for Star Wars' 50th anniversary states that 2027 will bring a year of "new project announcements, anniversary merchandise, dedicated fan events, archival releases, and reimagined Disney Parks and Cruiseline offerings." Exactly what these project announcements are remains to be seen, though it seems likely we'll get a sense of the franchise's future before next year is out.

With Ahsoka and Starfighter the only remaining live-action Star Wars TV and movie projects publicly announced, the time has certainly come for Lucasfilm's newly-installed co-president Dave Filoni to map out what's next. Reports suggest that of everything Lucasfilm has previously announced, the new movie/trilogy written by Dark Phoenix's Simon Kinberg is the one currently moving forward.

items.title: As Xbox Turns 25, CEO Asha Sharma Says 'A Single Person Will Soon Be Able to Wield Capabilities That Once Required Entire Nations'
items.description: Xbox chief Asha Sharma has discussed her vision of the video games industry's next 25 years, and suggested its future lies in small teams or individuals able to "wield capabilities that once required entire nations."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Xbox chief Asha Sharma has discussed her vision of the video games industry's next 25 years, and suggested its future lies in small teams or individuals able to "wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

Sharma's essay, posted today on X/Twitter ahead of Xbox's quarter century anniversary this weekend, seems to take pains not to explicitly reference A.I. by name. But in a section looking ahead to the future of the Xbox brand and video games in general, the huge role that Sharma apparently believes A.I. will play is made pretty clear.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," Sharma wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable trade-off of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break," Sharma continued. "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

It's hard to imagine that this version of the future could be possible without the heavy use of A.I. tools in game development — a topic that is still highly controversial among video game fans, even as it becomes all the more ubiquitous behind the scenes.

For industry watchers, though, and also for Xbox employees, Sharma's message also points to something else: a vision of game creation that's far leaner than now in terms of financial cost and human investment. After a another year of brutal layoffs across the video games industry and within Xbox in particular, this concept will likely do little to reassure anyone currently at the games development coalface.

"I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays," Sharma concluded. "Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen."

Sharma oversaw 1,600 job losses within Xbox back in July of this year, and laid out a plan for a further 1,600 employees to be shed over the rest of this year. This led to the company shedding several game developers — small teams — like Double Fine and Ninja Theory and reorganizing beloved studios like id Software this fall.

The 25th anniversary of Xbox is on Sunday, 15 November.

items.title: Palworld Developer Pocketpair Gives Employees 5 Days Off to Play GTA 6
items.description: Palworld developer Pocketpair is giving its staff five days off to make their way through GTA 6.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Palworld developer Pocketpair is giving its staff five days off to make their way through GTA 6.

“All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA 6 launches,” the company said in a tweet. The company also shared a letter it presumably sent out internally to workers at the studio.

“To all employees,” the letter started. “On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin.

“At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention. Therefore, after careful consideration, we have decided that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto VI will be granted a special five-day holiday.

The holiday period starts on GTA 6 launch date, November 19, and ends on November 23. “During this period, employees will be excused from their regular duties and are instead encouraged to take a business trip to Vice City,” the letter said.

“We hope everyone enjoys their time away from the office and returns safely from their travels.”

All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches.

Please see the attached notice for details. https://t.co/qJjJ7IvhhY

— Palworld (@Palworld_EN) November 12, 2026

Pocketpair boss Takuro Mizobe tweeted to confirm he'll be making the most of the special holiday, saying: "Of course, I’ll be taking a break for a while to play GTA6 too!"

Pocketpair isn’t the only company talking about GTA 6’s launch. The developer behind Wardogs encouraged its players to “go play GTA 6” and come back to the game after its next big update. Palworld developer Pocketpair is giving its staff five days off to make their way through GTA 6.

“All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA 6 launches,” the company said in a tweet. The company also shared a letter it presumably sent out internally to workers at the studio.

“To all employees,” the letter started. “On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin.

“At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention. Therefore, after careful consideration, we have decided that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto VI will be granted a special five-day holiday.

The holiday period starts on GTA 6 launch date, November 19, and ends on November 23. “During this period, employees will be excused from their regular duties and are instead encouraged to take a business trip to Vice City,” the letter said.

“We hope everyone enjoys their time away from the office and returns safely from their travels.”
